name: Korova Arms Phantom Frequency KA-12 'Ghost Note'
description:
A sonic weapon that projects focused ultrasonic pulses at frequencies above human hearing. The Ghost Note's beam causes intense localized heating in tissue at the focal point, producing burns and internal damage without any audible warning. At maximum power, the ultrasonic focus can raise tissue temperature to 80°C at a depth of 3cm — sufficient to cook organs beneath the skin.

Korova Arms designed the KA-12 for covert operations where the cause of death must be untraceable by conventional forensic methods. Ultrasonic tissue damage mimics the presentation of certain rare medical conditions — internal burns without external marks, organ damage without penetrating trauma. A Ghost Note kill requires a medical examiner specifically trained to identify ultrasonic heating patterns.

The weapon is disguised as a commercial ultrasonic range-finder, complete with functional range-finding capability. The lethal mode is accessed through a BCI-authenticated interface that does not appear on the device's physical controls.
legality: Officially classified as a commercial surveying tool
specifications:
caliber: N/A — focused ultrasonic beam
effective_range: 5-50 meters
rate_of_fire: Continuous beam, 5-second exposure for lethal effect
capacity: 20 lethal-duration exposures per charge
weight: 1.2 kg
power_source: Integrated power cell, 8 hours standby / 100 seconds active beam
tactical_use: The Ghost Note is deployed for deniable assassination and covert elimination. The weapon's disguise as commercial equipment allows operators to carry it through security checkpoints unchallenged. Engagement protocol involves sustained beam exposure from close range — the operator holds the 'range-finder' pointed at the target for 5 seconds, during which the target experiences a sensation of intense warmth that rapidly escalates to searing internal pain. By the time the target reacts, the damage is done.
cultural_context: Korova Arms' entire product philosophy centers on weapons that officially do not exist. The Ghost Note is their most commercially successful non-weapon, with units circulating through intelligence communities worldwide. The device's dual-function design — legitimate surveying tool and covert weapon — represents the ultimate expression of plausible deniability. Operators who carry the KA-12 can truthfully state they are carrying a range-finder.
story_hooks: An autopsy revealed internal burns consistent with ultrasonic heating in a person who died of apparent organ failure. The medical examiner has identified the pattern in three other recent deaths. Someone is using a Ghost Note systematically, and the victims are all connected to the same corporate board.

Korova's disguise has been compromised — a security company has developed a scanner that detects the KA-12's ultrasonic emitter, distinguishing it from legitimate range-finding equipment. Korova is scrambling to redesign their concealment before their entire product line becomes detectable.

physical_description.visual_profile: Compact handheld device resembling a professional laser rangefinder or surveying instrument. Sleek, almost clinical in appearance—something a corpo surveyor or construction tech would carry without question. Cylindrical body with a slightly tapered front section housing the transducer array. The silhouette screams 'legitimate tool' rather than weapon.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 18 cm | Width: 6.5 cm | Height: 7 cm | Transducer face: 4 cm diameter
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light in hand—1.2 kg distributed evenly. Feels professional and balanced, like quality surveying equipment. The low weight makes it easy to aim and sustain beam exposure, disguising its lethality.
physical_description.primary_material: Aircraft-grade aluminum alloy chassis with reinforced polymer casing around the resonance chamber. Internal transducer array is piezoelectric ceramic matrix with acoustic lens focusing system.
physical_description.finish: Brushed aluminum with matte black polymer accents. Anti-glare coating on the front optical section. Weathered in the field—fine micro-scratches consistent with professional equipment that sees regular use.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray with matte black grip zone and lens surround. Subtle Korova Arms branding in silver on the side panel. Looks corporate-neutral, deliberately forgettable.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized non-slip polymer with subtle grip ridges. Textured like genuine surveying equipment—professional, ergonomic, slightly tacky to prevent slipping during sustained aiming.
distinctive_features: Fake LED readout window displaying 'range' and 'distance' metrics—updated in real-time for authenticity
Small adjustment dial on top (labeled 'resolution') that actually controls ultrasonic frequency calibration
Heat vents disguised as measurement ports along the sides
Transducer lens coated in anti-reflection material giving it a faint amber tint
Battery indicator light (green/yellow/red) positioned like standard equipment diagnostics
Subtle wear pattern around the trigger area from sustained operation
Micro-adjustment screws for acoustic focusing, visible but meaningless to untrained observers
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: KOROVA ARMS logo stamped in silver on upper left side. Serial plate mounted on the base grip zone (encrypted quantum authentication module beneath cosmetic serial). Small regulatory markings indicating 'Professional Surveying Equipment - ISO Compliant' in multiple languages. Manufacturing date code subtle and authentic-looking.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but well-maintained. Minor scratches and scuff marks consistent with equipment that has seen regular professional deployment. Lens slightly dusty, grip showing natural wear from extended holds. No obvious battle damage—maintenance protocols keep it in survey-grade condition. Occasionally shows residual thermal discoloration around the transducer lens (barely perceptible) after extended operations.
